title: Microsoft Teams: two presenters can share screens or windows at the same time in meetings
summary: The roadmap facts, rollout notice and documented sharing controls are substantially supported. Hold for the unsupported assurance that no budget control applies and the claims that the organiser's role and meeting option are undocumented, despite explicit descriptions in the notice and PowerShell reference.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing sharing policies and informing users and support teams.
claims.quote: Review your organization's sharing policies and inform users and support teams about the new experience.

claims.claim: The notice states that no compliance considerations were identified.
claims.quote: No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

claims.claim: The notice describes no new data storage or processing.
claims.quote: Participants can see both shared content streams simultaneously, making it easier to compare and discuss content from different presenters.

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor the notice describes an identity or authentication change.
claims.quote: This capability will be enabled for all meetings by default, allowing a second presenter to start sharing without requiring the first presenter to stop.

claims.claim: The notice provides no detailed role eligibility rules for becoming the second presenter.
claims.quote: allowing a second presenter to start sharing without requiring the first presenter to stop.

claims.claim: The described sharing action is initiated by a presenter.
claims.quote: allowing a second presenter to start sharing

claims.claim: Neither supplied record describes automated or agent-driven sharing.
claims.quote: Two presenters can share a screen or window at the same time in a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how the second stream appears on other clients.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous two presenters multiple screenshare AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center meeting option license pricing mobile; Teams simultaneous sharing mobile organizer. Opened content-sharing guidance and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; no second-stream client presentation details found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Feature-specific licensing is not yet published, so the licensing model is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneously presenters license sharing; Teams simultaneous sharing licensing meter budget cap. Opened Manage Teams licenses, Microsoft Teams add-on licenses and both cited Learn pages; found no simultaneous-sharing-specific licence requirement.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Neither supplied record names a meter, and no feature-specific meter was found in Microsoft Learn.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous sharing licensing meter budget cap; Teams simultaneous two presenters multiple screenshare license pricing. Read both records, Teams licensing and add-on licensing pages, content-sharing guidance and the cmdlet reference; no feature-specific meter found.

claims.claim: No cap or budget control applies because no meter is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous sharing licensing meter budget cap. Opened Teams licensing, add-on licensing, content-sharing guidance and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; none states that no cap or budget control applies. An undocumented meter does not establish this conclusion.
claims.fix: Remove 'No cap or budget control applies, because no meter is documented.'

claims.claim: No Teams admin center path for the multiple-screenshare setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center; Teams multiple screenshare meeting option role. Opened Manage meeting policies for content sharing and Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy. The former gives no multiple-screenshare path; the latter documents PowerShell but no admin-center navigation.

claims.claim: MicrosoftTeams PowerShell supports Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AllowMultipleScreenshare $false to disable multiple screenshare for the policy, subject to the release caveat.
claims.quote: It controls whether Multiple Screenshare is on or off for the entire tenant or for a particular user. ... $false: MultiVBSS meeting options are not available (hidden) for the organizer.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference warns that the multiple-screenshare setting has no effect because the feature has not been fully released.
claims.quote: This feature has not been fully released yet, so the setting will have no effect.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The reference does not explicitly identify AllowMultipleScreenshare as the control for roadmap item 80239 or MC1528014.
claims.quote: Searched: AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center; Teams multiple screenshare meeting option role. Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and searched its text for AllowMultipleScreenshare, MC1528014 and 80239; the parameter exists but neither identifier appears.

claims.claim: Content-sharing policies are at Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Content sharing.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Go to the Content sharing section.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -ScreenSharingMode <value> controls the existing screen-sharing mode.
claims.quote: You can also use the Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy cmdlet to control the content sharing settings. Set the following parameters: ... ScreenSharingMode

claims.where: controls[1].governs and scope; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Screen sharing mode is a per-user policy governing whether a user can share a desktop or window.
claims.quote: This setting is a per-user policy. The setting controls whether a user can share a desktop and window in a Teams meeting.

claims.claim: The cited documentation does not explain Screen sharing mode's specific interaction with simultaneous sharing or describe it as a presenter-count control.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous two presenters multiple screenshare AllowMultipleScreenshare; AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center. Read content-sharing guidance and ScreenSharingMode in Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy; neither describes an interaction or presenter-count setting.

claims.where: Scope: Who configures it; Open questions
claims.claim: The notice does not name a specific administrator role for its tenant-level control.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams multiple screenshare meeting option role; AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center. Read MC1528014 and the cmdlet's parameter description, which says Tenant Admins but does not name a specific administrative role for the notice's control.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not named the role needed to configure the organiser's per-meeting option.
claims.quote: Meeting organizers will also have a meeting option to control whether multiple presenters can share simultaneously in an individual meeting.
claims.fix: Replace 'Microsoft has not named the role needed for either.' with 'The notice identifies meeting organisers for the per-meeting option but does not name a specific administrator role for the tenant-level control.'

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described the organiser's meeting option in any page found.
claims.quote: $true: Multiple VBSS (MultiVBSS) meeting options are available and enabled for the organizer. ... $false: MultiVBSS meeting options are not available (hidden) for the organizer.
claims.fix: Replace the final sentence with 'The AllowMultipleScreenshare reference describes Multiple VBSS meeting options as available and enabled for the organiser when true, and hidden when false; it also warns that the setting currently has no effect.'

claims.claim: The prose gives Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > Content sharing as the path for reviewing each policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Meetings > Meeting policies. ... Select the policy that you want to edit. ... Go to the Content sharing section.
claims.fix: Replace the parenthetical path with 'Teams admin center > Meetings > Meeting policies > policy > Content sharing', matching the existing controls row.

claims.claim: The page rates impact medium although its rationale describes a change to default behaviour, which the standard defines as high impact.
claims.quote: impact: "medium"; rationale: 'Microsoft's notice says it is enabled for all meetings by default'. The standard defines high impact as 'most users, or a change to default behaviour'.
claims.fix: Set impact to 'high' and replace the impact rationale with: High. Microsoft's notice says the capability is enabled for all meetings by default, changing default screen-sharing behaviour.

claims.claim: No dedicated Microsoft Learn feature page was found beyond the parameter reference and surrounding sharing guidance.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams simultaneous two presenters multiple screenshare AllowMultipleScreenshare admin center meeting option license pricing mobile; Teams multiple screenshare meeting option role. Opened Set-CsTeamsMeetingPolicy and content-sharing guidance; no dedicated simultaneous-sharing page found.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap record nor MC1528014 names a licence requirement.
claims.quote: Organizations will have tenant-level admin control to determine whether simultaneous sharing is available to their users. Review your organization's sharing policies and inform users and support teams about the new experience.

claims.claim: The notice announces a tenant-level control but gives no location for it.
claims.quote: Organizations will have tenant-level admin control to determine whether simultaneous sharing is available to their users.

claims.claim: The notice recommends communication and training for users and support teams.
claims.quote: Review your organization's sharing policies and inform users and support teams about the new experience.
claims.fix: Replace the indirect-cost sentence with 'The known cost is indirect: admin time to review sharing settings and communication for users and support teams, as the notice recommends.' The notice recommends informing users, not training.
